docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: • The purpose of this data sheet is to understand the thought process and the inner workings of the PCB board that connects all the other components in the Heart Rate Monitor project.

docs.title: Project Summary
docs.text: • The purpose of our project is to create a working heart rate monitoring system that will be displayed, as well as heard through speakers. The full report of the general workings of the heart rate monitor can be found here: team report.

docs.title: My Contribution
docs.text:
• The purpose of my PCB is to be the bridge between all other boards. My board will obtain the raw data from one of the boards, compile and simplify it, then send it out to the other two boards. Since my board will be connected to all others, a separate yet integrated temperature-sensing circuit has been added to indicate when the board gets too hot.
  • To review the general concept behind the design of the board, you can review it in the "Block Diagram" section of the datasheet.
  • To review the component selection process for the board, you can review it in the "Component Selection" section of the datasheet.
  • To review the bill of materials behind the chosen materials of the board, you can review it in the "BOM" section of the datasheet.
  • To review the schematic behind the design of the board, you can review it in the "Schematic" section of the datasheet.
  • To review the power budget, you can review it in the "Power Budget" section of the datasheet.

docs.title: Component Selection
docs.text:
Voltage Regulator

  1. Texas Instruments UA7805CKCS Voltage Regulator

    • $1.63/each
    • link to product
    Pros Cons Established 7805 style regulator design Linear regulator heat losses still apply Fixed 5 V output requires no ouput voltage adjustment Confirm the exact part's datasheet, package, and availability before ordering Through hole versions are suitable for prototyping May cost more than other 7805 compatible options

  2. STMicroelectronics L7805BV Voltage Regulator

    • $1.08/each
    • Link to product
    Pros Cons Provides fixed 5 V suitable for Curiosity Nano and MCP6004 Needs an input voltage above 5 V, with sufficient headroom. Through-hole TO-220 package is relatively easy to solder Excess input voltage is dissipated as heat. Includes overtemperature and short-circuit protection The 1.5 A rating does not guarantee that it can deliver 1.5 A continuously without appropriate thermal management.

  3. NTE960 Voltage Regulator

    • $1.50/each
    • Link to product
    Pros Cons Fixed 5 V output Lower current rating than proposed 1.5 A regulator Through hole package is convenient for assembly Must verify that the actual system current is within its rating. Its 1 A output rating may be sufficient for a modest logic board Still require thermal analysis Choice: Option 2: STMicroelectronics L7805BV Voltage Regulator

Rationale: The L7805BV was selected for its fixed 5 V output. Its simple design makes it easy to integrate into the PCB. Its through-hole package also makes assembly easier, and I already own the component.

External Power Supply

  1. 12 V, 1 A DC Wall Adapter External Power Supply

    • $7.20/each
    • link to product
    Pros Cons Supplies up to 1 A at 12 V A linear 5 V regulator will dissipate substantial heat dropping 12 V to 5 V Convenient for a stationary prototype The adapter's connector and polarity must match your board Provides more input voltage than a 5 V rail requires Its current capacity must be checked against the calculated system load

  2. Avue 12V, 1 A Adapter External Power Supply

    • $9.99/each
    • Link to product
    Pros Cons A readily purchasable wall adapter. Same linear regulator heat concern as option 1. Rated for 12 W of output power. The connector and polarity must be verified. Suitable for evaluating a stationary prototype if the connector and electrical specifications match. Must have sufficient current remaining after accounting for all loads.

  3. Truetone 1 SPOT 9 V Adapter External Power Supply

    • $27.99/each
    • Link to product
    Pros Cons Supplies 9 V DC and is intended for continuous equipment power. More expensive than the other candidates. Lower input voltage than 12 V reduces the regulator's voltage drop and heat. Its center-negative connector may not match your board. Listed output current is 1.7 A. A linear regulator will still dissipate heat, and actual current demand must be calculated.

Choice: Option 3: Truetone 1 SPOT 9 V Adapter External Power Supply

Rationale: The 9 V adapter was selected because it provides a practical power source for a stationary prototype. It produces less heat than a 12 V adapter in a linear regulator. It can provide consistent power without requiring a battery. Its polarity, connector, and current capacity must be verified before use.

PCB Temperature Sensor

  1. Microchip MCP9700 Temperature Sensor

    • $0.42/each
    • link to product
    Pros Cons Analog output can be read by the PIC's ADC. The PIC must convert and interpret the analog voltage. Operates from a 2.3–5.5 V supply. Measurement accuracy must be considered when choosing the cutoff temperature. Temperature range is −40°C to 150°C. Additional circuitry is needed if the sensor must directly trigger a hardware cutoff.

  2. Analog Devices DS18B20 Temperature Sensor

    • $2.83/each
    • Link to product
    Pros Cons Digital 1-Wire interface uses only one data pin. Requires firmware to read and interpret the digital data. Typical accuracy is ±0.5°C from −10°C to +85°C. Uses a digital interface rather than a direct analog ADC input. Supports programmable resolution and configurable temperature alarms. A separate power-disconnection mechanism is still needed for an independent failsafe.

  3. TMP102 Temperature Sensor

    • $5.95/each
    • Link to product
    Pros Cons Supplies 9 V DC and is intended for continuous equipment power. More expensive than the other candidates. Lower input voltage than 12 V reduces the regulator's voltage drop and heat. Its center-negative connector may not match your board. Listed output current is 1.7 A. A linear regulator will still dissipate heat, and actual current demand must be calculated.

Choice: Option 1: MCP9700 Temperature Sensor

Rationale: The MCP9700 was selected because its analog output can be read directly by the PIC's ADC. This simplifies temperature monitoring and reduces interface complexity. It operates within a voltage range suitable for many low-voltage circuits. An additional threshold circuit is needed to trigger an automatic thermal shutdown.

Power Switching Components

  1. Texas Instruments TPS22919 Power Switch

    • $0.32/each
    • link to product
    Pros Cons Supports 1.6–5.5 V input and up to 1.5 A continuous current. Small SC-70 package is more difficult to solder than a through-hole part. Includes thermal shutdown and short-circuit protection. Requires a control signal to enable or disable the output. Provides controlled power-up and output discharge. Its built-in thermal shutdown is not a substitute for a separately specified board-temperature threshold.

  2. Texas Instruments TPS22917 Power Switch

    • $0.16/each
    • Link to product
    Pros Cons Offers a compact integrated power-switching solution. Confirm the exact current rating and operating voltage for the selected package. Has controlled turn-on and output-discharge functionality. Small package may be challenging to assemble. Can reduce the number of discrete switching components. Requires additional temperature-sensing and control circuitry for a defined PCB cutoff temperature.

  3. Texas Instruments TPS22991 Power Switch

    • $0.08/each
    • Link to product
    Pros Cons Integrated load-switch solution. Verify the exact input-voltage and current specifications before selection. Includes controlled turn-on and output-discharge features. Small surface-mount package requires careful PCB footprint and assembly. Offers another commercial option for comparison with the TPS22919. Does not replace a separately designed temperature-threshold circuit. Choice: Option 3: Texas Instruments TPS22991 Power Switch

Rationale: The TPS22919 was selected because it provides compact electronic power control. Its integrated design can reduce the number of separate components on the PCB. It also includes thermal shutdown and short-circuit protection for the switch itself. An external temperature-threshold circuit is still needed to disconnect the protected power rail when the PCB overheats.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This schematic is designed to support team 204's Heart Rate Monitor. Its purpose is to receive and compile information, then send it to two other PCBs. The Board shall consist of three different circuits. The first circuit is responsible for supplying power, with a blue LED indicating whether the power is on. The second circuit involves the microcontroller, and it will receive an analog signal from one board and send it to the other two boards. Finally, the third circuit is responsible for measuring the board's temperature and lighting a red LED if it gets too hot.
